lesson.subtitle: Lesson 4 -- Race Day
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Camillo Furlan Alfredini | Lesson 4 -- Race Day
lesson.grammar_point: present simple third person (he works, she doesn't drive, does he travel?)

listenings.text: Good afternoon, and welcome to race day! The race starts at two o'clock. Each driver does seventy laps. The pit lane opens at one thirty. Every team has one minute for a test in the pit lane. Please stay behind the yellow line. The track is very hot today, so the tires are very important. Enjoy the race!

Hi, I'm Marco, and I'm a mechanic on a Formula 1 crew. My job is the front left tire. In a pit stop, I change it in about two seconds. I travel to more than twenty countries every year. I don't drive the car, of course. The driver drives, and I work in the garage. I love my job, but I don't see my family a lot.

extra_audio.text: Marco works on a Formula 1 crew. He wakes up at six o'clock on race day. He checks the tires and the tools in the garage. At two o'clock, the race starts. In the pit stop, he changes the front left tire in two seconds. After the race, he goes back to the hotel, and he calls his family.

paras: Marco is thirty years old, and he is from Italy. He works on a Formula 1 crew. He is not the driver: he is a mechanic. His job is very small and very important. He changes the front left tire.

On race day, Marco wakes up at six o'clock. He has breakfast with the crew at the hotel. At eight, he goes to the garage. He checks the tires, the tools and the helmet of the driver. He doesn't talk a lot in the morning. He is very focused.

The race starts at two. There are seventy laps. In the pit stop, Marco changes the tire in about two seconds. After the race, he goes back to the hotel, and he calls his family. Does he like his job? Yes, he does. He loves it.
